notes.title: Announcement: Sector Unknown - A Sci-Fi cRPG
notes.content:
As one of the developers on Deadwater Saloon, I would like to take a moment and announce my next game, a cPRG titled Sector Unknown.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2734270/Sector_Unknown/

After creating quite a few strategy games as an indie (and mostly solo) developer, I decided, perhaps quite insanely, to create an cRPG instead. This is the genre that I find myself playing and enjoying the most, from classics such as Baldur’s Gate 2, Fallout 2, Fallout New Vegas, Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, to more contemporary games such as Pillars of Eternity, Outer Worlds, Colony Ship, Trudograd, Underrail, and Encased. In short, I really, really like RPGs, and especially ones that use an isometric angle of gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915433/3374af1c0cc528a1be0d896da5acbaa0f34aca43.png[/img]

Sector Unknown is sort of my love letter to both the classics and the contemporaries. I think I’m better suited for telling a story than number crunching strategy games (as evidenced by my mixture of reviews in that genre).

After three years working part-time (well almost full time) on the systems, the game is close to complete on features (movement, inventory, party management, quests, dialogue, crafting, combat, itemization, space flight, etc). I’m aiming to have a demo for the game completed in a month or so. It’s close to completion now, but I’m still not happy with the tutorial level. What I do not want is for it to be a barrier to entry like the much-maligned temple tutorial level in Fallout 2 (I almost never experienced the rest of that fantastic game due to being so turned off by the temple).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915433/7a97d24f2231b65d4036fb79fdf14b05eab5419e.png[/img]

The goal for this game is to launch into Early Access. I intend to have over half of the game completed by that EA launch with full launch occurring 6-9 months after that. The idea to do an EA launch was not one taken lightly, but one thing I have found with my past launches is that just when I think a game is bug-free and ready for a seamless launch, players will find new and interesting ways to break things – leading to frantic post-launch schedule of rushing out bug-fixes and patches. I think this way is better. Launch into Early Access and take player feedback over time so that I can get everything sorted for a smooth launch after that. 

The other factor is budget. Right now, I do not have the armor or model system in place for player characters and NPCs. These are assets. This will change before Early Access as I have the models done (with no armor or clothing yet), but even after that, I suspect I will need some of the additional revenue from EA launch to finish the last 2-3 planets (as mentioned I aim to have 3-4 story planets complete for EA launch, with the first one ready for the demo in the coming month or so).

I hope people will wishlist and follow this game. It’s always been a dream of mine to create a sci-fi cRPG, and there doesn’t seem to be many on the market except for Colony Ship (which I completed three times). So I hope there’s a market for something like this, a game taking inspiration from early Bioware and some of the great current game developers on the market today.

I will continue to provide updates in the next while, including game systems, story, ideas, and more. I really look forward to people's feedback and thoughts as well.

notes.title: Finalized Launch Date - September 14th, 2022
notes.content:
Hey all, so we've seen from reviews and comments that most people playing the demo or prologue are having fun - but that the feeling is also there that the game needs just a bit more polish and shine (primarily in the animations department).

So we decided to move the new launch date to September 14th - this provides a few more weeks to focus on the feedback (which has been amazing, thank you) and get all of it implemented in the game.

Thanks again and please keep the feedback coming! I enjoy interacting with all of you and hearing your great ideas.

notes.title: Deadwater Saloon - Updates (August 7-8)
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42687967/30a4f32468764db90a09485ef2bfd748a3299bbb.png[/img]

Thanks for the continued feedback everyone, really appreciate it. 

Here are some additional changes made August 7 and August 8 based on people's feedback.

[list]
[*]Option to invert middle mouse-button for camera control
[*]Increased base action points to 4
[*]People now lie down in brothel beds
[*]Option for more or less challenging townspeople on game start (options for townspeople are now either pleasant or assholes)
[*]Added a third speed option for the game
[*]Reduced base upkeep but added upkeep to furniture
[*]When building an item, the rotation will be stored from the last item you set down
[*]Option exist to pay townfolk to be your friend
[*]Trapper and first house is built sooner in town (within the first hour or so of in-game time)
[*]Increased other business revenue significantly
[*]Attributes cannot be assigned past 80 on the new game start screen
[*]Lighting shaders of vultures fixed so they no longer glow at night
[*]Wall items like pictures and animal heads now outline when building or editing them
[*]Fixed bug where items built first and then walls built around the items would prevent items from being moved around after in edit mode
[*]Fixed bug with person sleeping in brothel bed when first built
[*]Reduced animal traffic slightly
[*]Top floor can now be placed more seamlessly (full version of game)
[*]Fixed bug with Bacon being locked despite being a tier one research item (will only work on new games)
[*]While placing or moving furniture, the option now exists to press shift and have items snap to the grid - for all the neat-freaks out there!
[*]A prompt comes up if a business with new items for research is built - this is to help avoid confusion of some players when they buy whiskey but cannot sell it (they need to research at least one recipe first).
[/list]

As always, lots more to come.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42687967/24220e42e6ac9baaa24158981cdf76027074beca.png[/img]

notes.title: Deadwater Saloon - Updates (August 5-6)
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42687967/7867773645d011b2536abcf00137213db30ee936.png[/img]

Thanks for the feedback all, both positive and negative.

Here's the changes made thus far over the last two days in response to reviews and forum posts:

[list]
[*]Fixed bug with achievements not triggering anytime after a game is saved or loaded 
[*]NPCs have no chance of being a nemesis right after moving in
[*]Can now attempt to befriend nemesis characters (this was restricted before)
[*]Removed opinion penalties from failing in befriending a townsperson
[*]Lowered cost of road repair from $150 to $50
[*]Fixed a bug on character creation screen where attributes could be increased past 100
[*]Added more labels to show that town supplies will not replenish if the road is in disrepair or blockaded
[*]Night sky is not so black - natural lighting added during nighttime
[*]Fixed small bug with birds sometimes freezing
[*]Increased frequency of travelers coming into saloon
[*]Slight increase in low-level booze prices
[*]Increased starting attribute points for player characters
[*]Adjusted town growth for the prologue and demo versions of the game
[*]Fixed several reported bugs with events
[/list]

More to come.

notes.content:

The changes have been numerous, including a revamping of the staffing system, more events, game start options, and a plethora of smaller bug fixes (though the edit furniture bug still exists and is continually being worked on).

Note that older save files may not work with this new update. 

We hope you enjoy and please continue to send us any feedback you might have.

notes.title: Join us Feb 21 during Steam Next Fest
notes.content:
At long last, here we are. At the point where things begin to take shape, and sly yokels can outwit the city slickers who take them for simpletons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/4bb80d43f3ba9f3036c9ebb0907a5894cf63f042.png[/img]

Yes, we have a playable Demo.

Granted, it’s an Early Access one. So don’t be squattin’ with your spurs on. The game is still bakin’ in the oven, meanin’ we are lettin’ yea in, but with the caveat that this is a work in progress.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/9ff5434478f2d6f316ef2467577e998f37b3a360.png[/img]

We couldn’t deny the chance to take part in the Steam Next Fest (what’s wrong with a little self promotion?), nor the opportunity to engage directly with yourselves, the fine future players of our efforts.

We want, and need, your open and honest-to-god feedback! Mostly so we can better understand just what in the heck is workin’, and what in the heck is not! No holdin’ back now. We aim to please.

Just also remember to not interfere with somethin’ that ain’t botherin’ you none… 

… that’s us sayin’ that if you like it, that’s good to let us know too. ;)

Without further ado, muster your horses and covered wagons, and mark your calendars to join us this coming Monday February 21st for a stroll through town! Feel that open air, those big skies, and them lonesome prairies.

Meet some new neighbors movin’ into town, stock up with some drinks and foodstuffs, and serve an enclave of thirsty customers, both local and transient.

Don’t worry about bitin’ off more than you can chew. Your mouth is probably a whole lot bigger than you think.

We look forward to meetin’ yea!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/0a2e4a31f578132be407ac176fc884f17a7d6290.png[/img]

notes.title: Saloon Gets a Big Upgrade
notes.content:
Rather than parsing you fine barkeeps into isolation, we’ve decided it best to put you right smack dab in the middle of town.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/9185f48e79695cb36b85ced662d04a3caa3ee394.png[/img]

Now you’ll be next door neighbors with Friends and Enemies of townsfolk alike. You best wise up, and learn how to share space, cause they ain’t gonna put up with your bullshit antics for too long.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/b7f2f2aeb0b785f6a3495eb4240233587c9d7f7c.png[/img]

You’ll experience firsthand a sleepy frontier settlement blossoming into a boom town around yea. Don’t worry, as a cornerstone in the community, you will have the opportunity to wield influence, and wreak havoc or prosperity. We leave that up to you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/c27e17b309a7c6bf2f697c6e3896211b62e34859.png[/img]

But you’ll be so close to your fellows, they’ll be able to taste the tobacco smoke emanating from your outfit. You’ll build while having the town around you in full view.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/0fd5606a2519960b458e48f39ea1edc9f38822dd.png[/img]

And while you’re in your room, notice outside the windows?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/84eefa02ac9f21872a0e005709d8f0575e901f71.png[/img]

Yeah. You can see the town. Just remember though: if you can see them, they can see you.

The idea before was to have the Saloon Build mechanics on a slab of dirt apart from the town, so as to help you keep focused on the rigorous tasks at hand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/7d68c4a8626c7966ebe4e543a331891ac5ce882e.jpg[/img]

But after much deliberation, we decided, “Ta Hell with it!” And put you fine fortune-seeking pioneers into the melting pot. Things are funner that way, no?

Take our word for it. Things are better this way.

notes.title: Day in the life…
notes.content:
[i]“The cheapest and easiest way to become an influential man and be looked up to by the community at large, was to stand behind a bar, wear a cluster-diamond pin, and sell whiskey.”[/i]
-Mark Twain

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/0f13f4c7f27bfe5897bd969ee7ae184cbaa46a54.png[/img]

And so here we are, ladies and gentlemen, together on the sober side of the bar. Your domain. The barkeep. To help you better understand the rigours, we’re gonna spend some time with Viola James, a young barkeep at the tender age of 20.

As you can see, she’s already begun the process of building and managing her outfit, known as Firewater Saloon. She put up walls, and invested in wallpaper, rugs, furniture, proper storage and even a room all to herself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/9651a4756f64aea9affff015d22abfb238701aff.png[/img]

Viola’s gonna have to work hard to upkeep her outfit, and keep it stocked with the finest liquors. But the most important aspect of running an outfit is finding good staff, and building good relations with the townsfolk.

As the town grows around her, many townspeople arrive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/d96a6490d841e0c314cda0767d2aeda0cda4a42a.png[/img]

With each one of them being a potential customer, Viola is going to attempt to better her relationship with a man that goes by the name of Xander Wright. At present, Xander doesn’t think too highly of Viola. In fact, his Opinion of her is only measured at 45%.

So in an attempt to better things, Viola is gonna try and compliment ol’ Xander. She’s got some choices. But no matter which she chooses, as you can see, her chances of winning him over is very low (each hovering around an 18% success rate).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/44ad58fd0729224864873056822ada548e3f1c59.png[/img]

Dammit! Her attempt backfires… and he thinks even less of her than before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/eae36935071e1a4ad31ca2a440306fc8ce9d6958.png[/img]

Maybe next time Viola.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/21bf1b23ef652b76fc345b1fee4b088837828ea5.png[/img]

notes.title: What Kind Of Saloon Owner Will You Be?
notes.content:
[h1]The Choice Is Yours...[/h1]

Whiskey drinking shit-kicker? Seductive charlatan? Studious or charismatic? Pious preacher? Ruthless manipulator?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/51cdb1e74601a32756d43563c801696011a1a97b.png[/img]

We like a wide range of possibilities, which is why we’ll let you decide how good-natured or rotten you wanna be. Just don’t come blaming us if you’re facing undesirable outcomes. You reap what you sow. And we believe in just desserts.

Not only will you get to name your Player Character, but also the Town, and your Saloon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/7de801560d520d3a98e029b1be7ef11fedf5d8d4.jpg[/img]

Here we have we have Franklin Mitchell, who will live in Bittervale. His outfit will be named Aces High Saloon. We’ve chosen a Handsome modifier, which gives a boost to two Attributes that may help him while he braves the frontier. Notice how his Savoir Faire and Seduction ratings are now at 30, while the rest remain at 10.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/39df777671352792cb8555bc65424642b4267897.jpg[/img]

Or would you rather be Captivating? With a boost to Drama and Leadership Attributes? It’s a tough call. Different Attributes will determine success in the face of different obstacles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/526c85bc40fb7b0910e8ec316b8b195f917f423c.jpg[/img]

Here we have Spring Thompson. We’ve selected the Compassionate modifier, which gives a boost to Medicine and Theology. Nothing like an amateur doctor with faith (Theology)! But also notice that we have now spent the Attribute Points. You start with 20, and can dispense them among the Attributes at will. So spend wisely. Here, Spring has an uptick in her Muscle rating (20), and Mixology (20). Why not have the capability to manhandle disruptive clientele and be better at mixing drinks?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/7ffca04c874508cb2542d75ca497979527b9fd26.jpg[/img]

And here, we’ve increased Spring’s age. Instantly, you are given more Attribute Points to spend, which we have used to uptick several more Attributes. Abstraction (20), Gambling (20), Savoir Faire (20). But also notice there’s a cost to Spring’s Health, which opens up a whole other set of circumstances and realities.

But we will save that for another time.

notes.title: Forging Your Way in the Wild West…
notes.content:
If like us, you’re lookin’ for an experience with the depth and sweeping grandeur of the wild west, while also havin’ a rootin-tootin good time, then grab the brandy and keep your rifles handy, 'cause we’re heading deep into the western frontier.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/72107b950d9774193e7886e9aa12e95c6e6a235e.png[/img]

Not only will you build and manage your own outfit, but you will interact with staff, customers and townspeople of all walks and dispositions. Some will become your friends, perhaps even allies. Others will surely not. It won’t always be easy, but you will be able to take all kinds of matters into your own hands, or simply carry on and let things fester out of sight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/6e61da8b36b6a65245513fed178179746059030c.png[/img]

Be wary though, for bandits rove the countryside, and as the town grows, the encroaching eyes of the law are ever watchful. Consequences can be dire. Always remember; there are multiple ways to skin a cat. Not that we condone that kind of behaviour, only feel compelled to let you decide.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/3aa6bb6dc2eca538896ae16a60e0fca98071560f.png[/img]

[h2]Our Goal[/h2]

We began work on Deadwater Saloon with a shared desire to play a management simulator in the wild west. Only, we had wishes to expand the traditional management sim to encompass a more immersive experience. We wanted to not only manage drinks, food, upkeep and decorum, but also a player character and their relationships, day to day struggles, and sanity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/c0060a995ebc28c155fd0ca93a132da251948355.png[/img]

We want the town to be a character unto itself. Settlers and townspeople will move into town, becoming affected and responding to your saloon and life choices. We are building a robust ecosystem within which to thrive and survive, or be overrun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371455/0d8fac20a3288505e586cf6a20f623d32990d4af.png[/img]

What has resulted is what we believe is an impactful experience. Not only with satisfying mechanics, but a satisfying emotional journey as well.

[h3]We can’t wait to continue sharing our development journey![/h3]
